field:rack::ui::Menu::activeEntry.finding: P0: Menu.active_entry returns wrapper(native.activeEntry) (native/bindings/ui/ui.cpp:298). Rack never clears activeEntry when that entry is removed or deleted; it only compares the pointer (Rack src/ui/MenuItem.cpp:21,68,73). After the active item is detached and closed, or request_delete()d and the menu stepped, reading active_entry hands a dangling pointer to wrapper(), which falls through to the external path and calls Rack's WeakPtr::set(native) (native/bindings/widget/managed.cpp:325-332), which dereferences ptr->weakHandle: a use-after-free that RackPy introduces. Smallest fix: track the entry like TextField prev/next_field (clear activeEntry from the entry's onDestroyed, ui.cpp focusField) or only return it if it is still a child of the menu; add a test that deletes the active entry and reads active_entry.

field:rack::ui::Menu::parentMenu.finding: P1: Rack's Menu::parentMenu is a public writable field (SDK include/ui/Menu.hpp:12), but RackPy makes it read-only (native/bindings/ui/ui.cpp:295). The notes and docs (docs/reference/ui.md ui-menus: 'So is parent_menu, which Rack 2.6.6 never sets') give no crash or ownership reason for refusing writes. Because Python can never set it, reading it always returns None and the field has no usable meaning. Smallest fix: allow writes with lifetime tracking, as focusField does for TextField prev/next_field (clear on the target's deletion), or document a real safety justification for the restriction.

method:rack::ui::Scrollbar::draw(const r.finding: P0: Rack's Scrollbar::draw does assert(dynamic_cast<ScrollWidget*>(parent)) (Rack src/ui/Scrollbar.cpp:24-25), and Rack's asserts are on. RackPy lets a ui.Scrollbar be added to any parent and drawn, both through the Python draw binding and through the trampoline fallback (native/bindings/widget/trampoline.hpp:135-141). validateNativeDraw (native/bindings/widget/drawing.hpp:43-55) guards Svg and Framebuffer crashes but not this one, so a Scrollbar inside a FramebufferWidget aborts Rack on render. No cited test draws a Scrollbar. Smallest fix: refuse or skip native Scrollbar draw unless its parent is a ScrollWidget (add it to validateNativeDraw), document it, and test it.

method:rack::ui::Scrollbar::onButton(con.finding: P0: Rack's Scrollbar::onButton does assert(dynamic_cast<ScrollWidget*>(parent)) on a left press (Rack src/ui/Scrollbar.cpp:41-43). The on_button binding (native/bindings/widget/behavior.hpp BIND_EVENT) has no parent check, so ui.Scrollbar().on_button(ButtonEvent(button=0, action=PRESS)) aborts Rack. No cited test calls it. Smallest fix: refuse when the parent is not a ScrollWidget (OwnershipError), document it, and test both the jump-to-position behaviour and the refusal.

method:rack::ui::Scrollbar::onDragEnd(co.finding: P1: no cited test calls Scrollbar.on_drag_end (tests/ui/in_rack/test_widgets.py:337-369 has none). method:rack::ui::Scrollbar::onDragMove(c.finding: P0: Rack's Scrollbar::onDragMove does assert(dynamic_cast<ScrollWidget*>(parent)) (Rack src/ui/Scrollbar.cpp:71-72). The on_drag_move binding (native/bindings/widget/behavior.hpp BIND_EVENT) has no guard, so ui.Scrollbar().on_drag_move(DragMoveEvent(...)) on a detached bar, or one under any other parent, aborts Rack. The cited test only covers the attached case (tests/ui/in_rack/test_widgets.py:371-389). Smallest fix: refuse when the parent is not a ScrollWidget, document it, and test the refusal.
